artifacts.summary: Six-phase implementation of the shared gitignored-specs predicate library, the V13 classification gate with exit codes 8/9 in git-commit-scoped.sh, consumer exit-code handling in orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh and git-commit-phase.sh, the per-operation contract in git-staging-scope.md, and the redeploy/verification close.

completion_data.completion_summary: Added scripts/lib/specs-ignore-lib.sh (a shared gitignored-path predicate) and a V13 classification gate in git-commit-scoped.sh that distinguishes an all-ignored or partially-ignored specs tree (exit codes 8/9) from a genuine staging failure, with matching consumer handling in orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh and git-commit-phase.sh and a per-operation contract added to git-staging-scope.md. 12+83+84+321 test cases pass; the tree was redeployed and all seven edited/created files verified byte-identical against the deployed copy.

memory_candidates.content: Two source-store maintenance scripts in this codebase have invocation gotchas that cost real debugging time: (1) sync-manifest-scripts.sh derives its on-disk script inventory via `git ls-files`, not a filesystem walk -- a brand-new untracked file is invisible to --write/--check until explicitly `git add`-ed first. (2) generate-context-line-counts.sh refuses outright when invoked from the source-store scripts/ directory (agent-system/extensions/<ext>/scripts/), requiring invocation from the deployed tree (.claude/scripts/) instead, even though it always writes back to the source-store index-entries.json regardless of invocation site. A plan phase that adds a new scripts/lib/*.sh + scripts/tests/test-*.sh pair, or edits an indexed context/**.md file, should budget for staging the new files before running sync-manifest-scripts.sh --write, and for deploying before running generate-context-line-counts.sh --write (or simply trust that deploy-headless.sh's default mode already runs the line-count reconciliation as a side effect).

Before authoring new letter-prefixed test-case names (e.g. 'Y1-Y6', 'Z1-Z5') for a large, long-lived test suite, grep that suite for the proposed letter prefix first -- a plan authored without this check named new controls 'Y1-Y6' that silently collided with and would have shadowed a pre-existing Y1-Y6 (and separately Z1-Z18) case series already landed in the same file by earlier work. The suite's own letter-prefix history can span many unrelated features (V7/V8/V9/V10/V11 fixes each claimed their own letter run), so a reader cannot assume the next letter after the plan's own prior phase is free.

`git check-ignore -q` is index-aware: for a path that is already TRACKED, it reports 'not ignored' (exit 1) even when the path also matches a .gitignore rule, under both a parent-directory pattern and a direct file-level pattern. This makes it safe to use as the sole primitive for an 'is this untracked path ignored' classification gate without a separate tracked/untracked branch at the call site -- the index-awareness itself structurally prevents misclassifying an already-tracked, ignore-matching path. The same property means a caller that pre-stages a rename via `git mv` (rather than a plain `mv` plus a paired add) sidesteps any such gate entirely, since the destination is already an index entry by the time the gate runs.

sapience_notes.subject: git check-ignore -q index-awareness
sapience_notes.value: For an already-tracked path, `git check-ignore -q` reports 'not ignored' (exit 1) even when the path matches a .gitignore rule via a parent-directory pattern or a direct file-level pattern. This is a load-bearing, measured property (not assumed): it means the same primitive answers both 'is this untracked path ignored' and is structurally safe against misclassifying a tracked-but-ignore-matching path, with no separate branch needed at the call site.

sapience_notes.subject: git-mv vs plain-mv into a gitignored destination
sapience_notes.value: Measured directly: renaming a tracked file into an ignore-matched destination via `git mv` pre-stages the destination as a tracked index entry before any downstream commit-scoped script runs, so an ignore-aware classification gate correctly sees it as 'not ignored' and the rename commits normally (exit 0). The SAME rename via a plain `mv` plus a paired-pathspec commit (the actual call-site pattern this codebase's 'Rename and Directory-Move Staging' convention uses) DOES trip the gate: the destination is dropped as gitignored while the source's own deletion still lands as a normal fully-staged-deletion -- a different, and more representative, outcome than the git-mv probe alone would suggest.

sapience_notes.subject: sync-manifest-scripts.sh on-disk inventory source
sapience_notes.value: sync-manifest-scripts.sh derives its 'on-disk' script set via `git ls-files`, not a raw filesystem walk. A brand-new untracked file is invisible to both --write and --check until it is explicitly `git add`-ed into the index first -- staging (not committing) is sufficient.

sapience_notes.subject: generate-context-line-counts.sh invocation-site requirement
sapience_notes.value: generate-context-line-counts.sh refuses outright (with an explicit remedy message) when invoked from the source-store scripts/ directory (agent-system/extensions/<ext>/scripts/); it must be invoked from a deployed scripts/ tree (.claude/scripts/ or .opencode/scripts/). It always writes back to the source-store index-entries.json regardless of invocation site -- the deployed-tree requirement is purely about REPO_ROOT resolution, not about where the write lands. deploy-headless.sh's default mode already runs this reconciliation as a side effect of a normal redeploy.

sapience_notes.subject: Decision: dedicated drop ledger for an unambiguous-cause classification gate
sapience_notes.value: When adding a new pathspec-classification gate (V13) to git-commit-scoped.sh whose drop cause is definitively known and definitively benign (an untracked, gitignored path), the drop was recorded in its OWN dedicated ledger (ignored_dropped) rather than mirrored into the shared ambiguous-cause ledger (dropped_pathspecs) that an existing refusal gate (V6, exit 4) reads. Rationale: admitting a benign, well-understood drop into an ambiguous-cause ledger would re-impose exactly the failure-flavoured framing the new gate exists to remove. This is a reusable decision pattern for any future classification gate added to this same script: ask whether the drop's cause is ambiguous (shared ledger) or definitively known (dedicated ledger) before wiring it in.

sapience_notes.subject: Naming collision in a long-lived letter-prefixed test suite
sapience_notes.value: A plan's authoring-time instructions named new test-case controls 'Y1-Y6' without checking whether those letters were already in use; test-git-commit-scoped.sh already carried pre-existing Y1-Y6 (an earlier cached-untracking feature) and Z1-Z18 (an earlier containment feature) case series. Corrected by renaming to AA1-AA7 at implementation time. Constraint for future plan authoring against this specific suite: letters through Z are claimed; the next free letter-run is AB.
